questions.stem: A technically capable employee is new to a high-risk procedure and is uncertain about site expectations. Which leadership approach is most appropriate initially?

Avoid feedback so the employee develops independence through trial and error

The option 'Use the same level of direction indefinitely regardless of performance' does not apply the controlling principle for situational leadership to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

The option 'Avoid feedback so the employee develops independence through trial and error' does not apply the controlling principle for situational leadership to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

The underlying case is: A technically capable employee is new to a high-risk procedure and is uncertain about site expectations. Which leadership approach is most appropriate initially? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Provide clear direction and close feedback while building confidence, then reduce direction as demonstrated competence increases
Avoid feedback so the employee develops independence through trial and error
Use the same level of direction indefinitely regardless of performance
Delegate the task completely because technical experience guarantees site competence
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Effective leadership adapts support and direction to task competence and commitment rather than applying one fixed style.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Avoid feedback so the employee develops independence through trial and error' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling situational leadership principle.
The proposed response 'Use the same level of direction indefinitely regardless of performance' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling situational leadership principle.
The proposed response 'Delegate the task completely because technical experience guarantees site competence' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling situational leadership principle.

questions.stem: At a team-performance assessment, a supervisor proposes: "Penalize departments with high reporting rates". The underlying case is: A reward program increases reporting briefly, then reports fall when prizes stop. Which redesign is most likely to support durable participation? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Increase prize value while ignoring whether reports lead to action
Strengthen meaningful feedback, psychological safety, visible corrective action, autonomy, and recognition rather than relying only on prizes
Keep corrective-action status confidential so reporting remains competitive
Penalize departments with high reporting rates
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Extrinsic rewards can influence short-term behavior, but sustained participation depends on trust, purpose, response quality, and supportive system conditions.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Increase prize value while ignoring whether reports lead to action' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling intrinsic and extrinsic motivation principle.
The proposed response 'Keep corrective-action status confidential so reporting remains competitive' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling intrinsic and extrinsic motivation principle.
The proposed response 'Penalize departments with high reporting rates' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling intrinsic and extrinsic motivation principle.

questions.stem: At a delegation and accountability review, a supervisor proposes: "Keep the confusing procedure and require another acknowledgment signature". The underlying case is: An experienced operator makes an unintentional error within a confusing procedure; the same trap has affected others. Which response best reflects a just culture? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Apply the maximum penalty because any error requires identical punishment
Keep the confusing procedure and require another acknowledgment signature
Address the procedure and system contributors, coach the employee as appropriate, and distinguish human error from reckless behavior
Remove all individual accountability whenever a system weakness exists
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A just culture balances learning and accountability by differentiating human error, at-risk behavior, and reckless choices while correcting system weaknesses.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Apply the maximum penalty because any error requires identical punishment' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling just culture and accountability principle.
The proposed response 'Keep the confusing procedure and require another acknowledgment signature' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling just culture and accountability principle.
The proposed response 'Remove all individual accountability whenever a system weakness exists' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling just culture and accountability principle.

questions.stem: At a conflict-resolution session, a supervisor proposes: "Mandate immediate compliance without explaining purpose or testing feasibility". The underlying case is: Supervisors resist a new permit process because they believe it will delay work and were not involved in design. What should the change leader do? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Cancel the control because any resistance proves it is impractical
Mandate immediate compliance without explaining purpose or testing feasibility
Label dissenters as unsafe and exclude them from implementation planning
Engage affected supervisors, test the workflow, address valid operational concerns, explain the risk basis, and establish feedback during implementation
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Participation, transparent rationale, pilot testing, and feedback can resolve legitimate concerns and build ownership without surrendering the safety objective.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Cancel the control because any resistance proves it is impractical' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling change resistance principle.
The proposed response 'Mandate immediate compliance without explaining purpose or testing feasibility' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling change resistance principle.
The proposed response 'Label dissenters as unsafe and exclude them from implementation planning' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling change resistance principle.

questions.stem: At an organizational-design discussion, a supervisor proposes: "Require approval for every minor action while withholding decision authority". The underlying case is: A safety director delegates inspection scheduling to a coordinator. Which action preserves effective accountability? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Define authority, expected results, resources, reporting, and follow-up while retaining leadership responsibility for the system
Assign the work without providing priorities, time, or access to records
Delegate the task and stop reviewing performance because responsibility transfers completely
Require approval for every minor action while withholding decision authority
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Effective delegation includes clear outcomes and sufficient authority plus oversight. Senior responsibility for the management system is not eliminated by task assignment.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Assign the work without providing priorities, time, or access to records' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling delegation and accountability principle.

The proposed response 'Delegate the task and stop reviewing performance because responsibility transfers completely' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling delegation and accountability principle.
The proposed response 'Require approval for every minor action while withholding decision authority' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling delegation and accountability principle.

questions.stem: At a leadership-style review, a supervisor proposes: "Frame the dispute as a contest between safety and production with no shared interests". The underlying case is: Maintenance and production disagree about a shutdown needed to correct a serious hazard. Positions have hardened. Which intervention is most constructive? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Delay discussion until one side withdraws its concern
Refocus both groups on shared risk and operational objectives, clarify facts and constraints, and develop options using agreed decision criteria
Let the department with the larger budget decide without risk analysis
Frame the dispute as a contest between safety and production with no shared interests
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Interest-based problem solving uses shared goals, reliable information, and explicit criteria to develop options, rather than escalating positional conflict.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Delay discussion until one side withdraws its concern' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling conflict resolution principle.
The proposed response 'Let the department with the larger budget decide without risk analysis' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling conflict resolution principle.
The proposed response 'Frame the dispute as a contest between safety and production with no shared interests' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling conflict resolution principle.
